shared_context.content: A coloring function f : R^2 -> {red, green} satisfies the circumcenter-monochromatic property if for every noncollinear triple of points A,B,C in the Euclidean plane, whenever f(A)=f(B)=f(C), the circumcenter of triangle ABC also has that same color.
shared_context.label: Root hypothesis schema

shared_context.content: For a point C in R^2 and a real number r>0, the circle with center C and radius r is the set {P in R^2 : dist(P,C)=r}. Distances are Euclidean distances.
shared_context.label: Circle notation

shared_context.content: If three distinct points lie on a circle with center C, then they are noncollinear and the circumcenter of the triangle formed by those three points is C.
shared_context.label: Circumcenter fact

strategy_summary: Use a local circle-counting contradiction centered at two opposite-colored points. This differs from the failed attempts by avoiding any false global classification of circumcenter-closed subsets; the key bridge uses only hypotheses available in the 2-coloring setup, plus a finite-incidence bound between two explicitly chosen circles.
